name: pr-ui-compare
description: Generate synchronized Before and After UI GIFs and images for pull requests with Playwright.
author: Anas Bouzid

untrustedWorkspaces.description: PR UI Compare runs project install and development server commands.

languageModelTools.name: pr-ui-compare_createComparison
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Records the running application and produces GIF or PNG files that show a labeled Before and After side by side. Use this tool only when the user wants a visual artifact to look at or share, such as a GIF, a screenshot, a Before and After image, or a recorded demonstration of a UI fix. Do not use it to compare code, read a diff, summarize what changed against a branch or ref, review a pull request, or verify that a fix works. A request such as compare my fix on this branch to main is a code comparison and must be answered by reading the code, not by running this tool, unless the user asks for a GIF, images, screenshots, or something visual to look at. When it is unclear whether the user wants generated media, ask before running the tool. Animation is the default and must be used whenever the change the user needs to see is itself motion, including any interaction, hover, transition, loading sequence, resize, zoom, scroll, or state mutation. Use scenario.setupActions for page preparation that must finish before an animated GIF begins; it replays in both versions and is omitted from the GIF. Set outputMode to image when the subject is a settled state that holds still, even when reaching that state requires interactions. In image mode the actions are setup steps rather than the subject: they replay in both versions and a single PNG captures the settled final state, so any reachable app state can be compared as a still. When uncertain between the two output modes, always choose animation. The tool resolves a baseline Git ref into a detached worktree, starts both applications sequentially, and stores artifacts outside the repository. It creates and modifies no files in the user's repository, and it runs the start and install commands it is given. Never write a JavaScript, TypeScript, Playwright, or shell helper script. Border color, color scheme, layout, focus crop, and label corners are configurable.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Generate Before and After GIFs or PNGs of the running app when you want visual evidence of a UI change.

outputMode.description: Output type. animation is the default and is required whenever the change the user needs to see is the motion itself. image captures a single settled state as PNG files, and its actions are replayed as setup so the state being compared can be anywhere in the app, not just the initial route.

frameRate.description: Animated GIF frame rate. Defaults to 24. Use 30 for fast visual events; lower values reduce file size for slow motion. Not available in image mode.

colorScheme.description: Preferred browser color scheme for both versions. system disables emulation and uses host browser behavior. Defaults to system.

beforeColorScheme.description: Optional color scheme override for the Before browser.

afterColorScheme.description: Optional color scheme override for the After browser.

baseRef.description: Git branch, tag, or commit for the Before application, normally upstream/main or the PR target branch. The After application is always the current working tree, so this is the only side that can be pointed at a ref.

startCommand.description: Shell command that starts either application. Use {port} where a dynamically allocated port should be inserted.

readyUrl.description: HTTP URL polled until the application is ready. Use {port} for the allocated port.

installCommand.description: Optional dependency installation command run only in the temporary Before worktree.

route.description: Route opened before replay, such as /settings.

beforeLabel.description: Optional short label shown over the Before recording. The short commit SHA is appended automatically, so never write one here. Recommended form is the side, a bullet, then the ref, such as "Before • main", which renders as "Before • main (7c52123c)". A bare ref name such as "main" is also good. Omitting this uses the baseline ref. When the user states a label, use it exactly as given.

afterLabel.description: Optional short label shown over the After recording. The short commit SHA is appended automatically, so never write one here. Recommended form is the side, a bullet, then the branch, such as "After • fix-overflow", which renders as "After • fix-overflow (efc0fab4)". A bare branch name is also good. Omitting this uses the current branch. When the user states a label, use it exactly as given.

beforeLabelAlignment.description: Corner for the Before label. Defaults to top-left.

afterLabelAlignment.description: Corner for the After label. Defaults to top-right.

labelSize.description: Label font size in pixels. Omit this unless the user explicitly requests a specific label size. The default scales automatically so labels stay consistent and readable across output sizes.

borderColor.description: Six-digit hex color for pane frames, the divider, and unused resize canvas. Defaults to GitHub dark border #30363d.

focusLocator.description: Optional Playwright locator for the UI region to crop around throughout the recording, such as a menu bar or panel.

focusPadding.description: Padding in pixels around the focused UI region. Defaults to 16.

layout.description: Comparison arrangement. Keep auto unless side-by-side must be forced. Top-and-bottom output is selected only when the focused region is strictly greater than 3:1, and cannot be forced for narrower content.

name.description: Short description of the behavior being demonstrated.

setupActions.description: Optional page preparation that runs identically in both versions before synchronization and is omitted from animated output. Use clicks, navigation, input, scrolling, resizing, waits, and holds to reach a settled starting state. Camera zoom belongs in visible actions.

locator.description: Playwright locator string, preferably role=, text=, label=, or data-testid=.
Playwright locator string, preferably role=, text=, label=, or data-testid=.

width.description: Target viewport width for a resize action.

height.description: Target viewport height for a resize action.

resizeMode.description: Required for resize. Choose the outcome directly. keep-left-edge-fixed means only the right edge moves. keep-right-edge-fixed means only the left edge moves. keep-window-centered means both edges move simultaneously at the same rate and the window remains horizontally centered. For a shrink where the left edge must slide right and the right edge must not move, use keep-right-edge-fixed.

captureStrategy.description: How the resize transition is captured. stop-motion is the default: each output frame is captured at an exact viewport size, so fixed edges stay perfectly rigid and Before and After resize in exact lockstep. Use live to record the browser resizing in real time only when the user wants the true live resize behavior or reports that the stop-motion result differs from what they observe.

scale.description: Camera magnification for a zoom action. Defaults to 1.8 when a locator is provided. Use 1 without a locator to zoom back out.

prUiCompare.retentionDays.description: Number of days to keep temporary recordings and comparison sessions outside the repository.

prUiCompare.allowSystemBrowser.description: Allow fallback to installed Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge when managed Chromium is unavailable. Keep disabled on macOS to avoid launching applications from the system Applications folder.

prUiCompare.ffmpegPath.description: Path to an FFmpeg executable. When empty, the extension uses FFmpeg from PATH or the copy installed by the PR UI Compare: Install FFmpeg command.

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && npm run lint
scripts.test:e2e: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && npm run lint && npm-run-all -s test:e2e:animation test:e2e:image
scripts.test:e2e:animation: cross-env PR_UI_COMPARE_E2E=1 vscode-test --grep "records and renders a dirty working tree" --timeout 180000
scripts.test:e2e:image: cross-env PR_UI_COMPARE_E2E=1 vscode-test --grep "captures and composes final-state PNG images" --timeout 180000
